frequency_question: How often do central banks deploy incremental reserve ratio measures within any given four-month window under baseline liquidity conditions?
membership_rule: Includes any formal secondary reserve ratio or incremental cash reserve ratio imposed to mop up excess banking system liquidity. Excludes standard statutory reserve ratio adjustments applied uniformly across decades.
provenance_note: claims 120 cases from only 2 named (60.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 2 named instances in RBI history; extremely rare tool deployed only during acute, unexpected liquidity surges (e.g., post-demonetization or post-pandemic bond auctions/surpluses).
known_gaps: Other emerging markets use similar tools under different names (e.g., PBoC reserve requirement ratio tweaks), but RBI-specific structural frequency is the most relevant analogue.
skeleton: RBI monetary policy review cycles over 20 years (approx 120 policy reviews), yielding 2 occurrences of iCRR activation.
multiplier: 2 occurrences out of roughly 120 scheduled bi-monthly monetary policy windows where liquidity overhang necessitated targeted absorption.
validity_reason: Central bank operating frameworks and liquidity management toolkits evolve slowly over multi-year strategic horizons.
